msg: This page loads third-party scripts but carries no script inventory. 6.4.3 requires a written inventory of every script on the payment page, each with a business justification. Add a <!-- pci-script-inventory --> block listing each host.
Script host is not listed in the page's script inventory, so it is not an authorised script under 6.4.3.
Inventory entry has no usable business justification. 6.4.3 asks why each script is needed, in writing; placeholders do not count.
External payment-page script has no integrity= hash, so there is no method assuring the script has not been altered in transit or at the origin (6.4.3).
Payment-page script is loaded over plain http://. Integrity cannot be assured and the content can be rewritten on the wire.
integrity= is present but crossorigin= is missing, so the browser will not run the integrity check the way you expect on a cross-origin script.
Script URL points at a moving target (latest/next), so today's authorised script is not tomorrow's. Pin a version before hashing it.
A tag manager or session-recording loader can inject further scripts at runtime, which means the authorised list is decided outside this file. Container contents have to be inventoried too.
No Content-Security-Policy on this payment page. Without one there is no technical method confirming that only authorised scripts execute in the consumer's browser.
script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' or a wildcard, which authorises anything. That is the same as having no script authorisation at all.
Only Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only is set. Report-only blocks nothing; it records and lets the script run.
Inline script has no nonce= and no hash, so it can only run if the policy is loosened for every inline script on the page.

No change- and tamper-detection mechanism is declared for this page. 11.6.1 wants alerts on unauthorised modification of the HTTP headers and of the payment page content. Declare it in a <!-- pci-tamper-detection: ... --> line or set a CSP report endpoint.
Tamper detection is evaluated less often than every seven days. 11.6.1 asks for at least weekly evaluation, or the interval your targeted risk analysis defends.
This page still describes the payment-script requirements as future-dated or optional. They stopped being best practice and became mandatory on 2025-03-31.
This file cites a retired version of the standard. v4.0.1 is the only active version; v3.2.1 retired 2024-03-31 and v4.0 retired 2024-12-31.
